question.text: A physical quantity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> is found to depend on quantities <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>c</mi></math> by the relation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></math>. The percentage error in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn><mo>%</mo></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo></math> respectively. Then, the percentage error in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> is:

solution.text:
Given quantity is Q=a4b3c2.

The relative error in measuring Q is given by

ΔQQ=4Δaa+3Δbb+2Δcc   ...1

Hence, the required percentage error is given by

ΔQQ×100=4Δaa×100+3Δbb×100+2Δcc×100=4×3%+3×4%+2×5%=12%+12%+10%=34%
